_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its (non-)oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in the shared ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json manifest. Line splitting, line-ending policy and trailing-newline handling are exactly what this subset ITSELF defines — no third-party crate is authoritative over 'is this a text file's line structure' the way lopdf is authoritative over PDF or png is authoritative over PNG, so no oracle is registered here (see noOracleDecisions below).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: There is no credible third-party crate that is authoritative over plain-text line structure: line splitting on LF/CRLF, uniform-per-document line-ending policy and trailing-newline presence are exactly what THIS subset defines, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute independently. The closest candidate, the `csv` crate already linked for the tabular subsets, genuinely helps for a NARROW part of this: with quoting disabled and a delimiter byte that cannot appear in real text, its record reader independently confirms this subset's own line-boundary splitting on single-style (no mixed CR/LF/CRLF), NON-BLANK real content — but a standalone probe found `csv-core`'s NFA silently treats a zero-byte record as "not a record" and never emits it (confirmed unconditionally, not a `Terminator`-mode artifact), so it cannot cross-check the true line count on any real prose that has blank lines at all, which most real text does (the real fixture below has 80, measured). It cannot discharge a full differential comparison either way: it collapses LF/CR/CRLF into one undifferentiated boundary and never reports which terminator it saw, so it cannot confirm or refute this subset's central claim (LF vs CRLF vs trailing-newline presence). Confidence instead comes from specification vectors (CRLF/LF/mixed, no trailing terminator, a BOM, astral-plane characters, combining marks, and NEL/LS/PS explicitly NOT treated as separators — all carried directly in the feature file as literal byte-exact local:// fixtures) and the inverse law as a metamorphic property (apply a mutation, apply its computed inverse, the real document's projection must return to the original) plus an independently hand-written reference implementation of the mutation semantics in this subset's own oracle module, which never calls this subset's production `TxtSnapshot`/`TxtMutation` code.
